chunks: As for what Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb narrated, from ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad al-Qāsānī, from al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad, from Sulaymān ibn Dāwūd, from al-Nuʿmān ibn ʿAbd al-Salām, from Abū Ḥanīfah, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who committed zinā with a dead woman. He said: “There is no hadd upon him.”

So this report admits of two possibilities. One of them is that the meaning is: there is no fixed hadd upon him such that no other than it would be permissible in all circumstances, because we have already explained that iḥṣān and its absence are considered in this matter. So if he is muḥṣan, then the hadd is rajm, and if he is not muḥṣan, then the hadd is one hundred lashes; and this is not upon one single hadd.

And the other possibility is that the report is specific to one who had intercourse with his own wife after her death. In that case, the hadd is not carried out upon him, and he is given taʿzīr according to what the Imam sees fit.

key_terms.الرَّجْمَ: stoning as a prescribed punishment for a muḥṣan offender
key_terms.الْإِحْصَانُ: the state of being muḥṣan, which affects the legal ruling
key_terms.الْإِمَامُ: the authority who determines the discretionary punishment
key_terms.جَلْدَ مِائَةٍ: one hundred lashes as the prescribed punishment for a non-muḥṣan offender
key_terms.يُعَزَّرُ: he is subjected to discretionary punishment

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling in Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām on a man who has intercourse with a deceased woman?
ai.summary: This passage discusses a legal report concerning intercourse with a deceased woman and explains how it may be understood within Shia jurisprudence. The text presents two possible readings: either that there is no single fixed hadd in every case because the ruling varies by iḥṣān status, or that the report refers specifically to a man approaching his own wife after her death, in which case taʿzīr rather than hadd applies.
